archetype.name: Pocket Passer (vertical)
archetype.definition: A rhythm thrower from the pocket who rarely runs and is now driving the ball 10-plus yards downfield more often and more accurately than at any point in his career.

report.headline: Stroud's downfield aggression is real, and it's carrying a flawed offense
report.take:
Stroud is a pocket passer. He has never run much, and his value lives in what he does from the pocket past the sticks. What's different in 2026 is how often he goes there. His aggressiveness rate of 19.15 is the highest of his four seasons, up 6.3 points on last year, and the throws themselves are cleaner: his bad-throw rate fell from 16.8% to 11.7%, now ninth among 42 charted passers. That combination of more tight-window shots with fewer misses is why his yards per attempt rose 0.79 and his per-game yardage ranks third in the league.

The split that explains his season is depth. On throws of 10-plus air yards he has added 61.9 EPA. Everything under 10 has added 16.7, and throws behind the line have cost 12.6. His deep balls produce 0.724 EPA per attempt with a +9.3 CPOE. That is not a quarterback living on YAC or checkdowns. The offense around him gives him little help: the run game ranks 25th in EPA, and the screen game is a drain. Houston's passing ranks seventh while its rushing sits near the bottom, so Stroud is the offense.

The 3-5 record hides how well he has played since September. The first three weeks were poor (combined EPA in the red, all losses), but over the last five games he has averaged 0.337 EPA per dropback with a 3.6% sack rate, about double his season rate in efficiency. The losses since then came in shootouts the defense couldn't hold: it ranks last in explosive passes allowed. The one dud in that stretch, a 153-yard day against the Giants, came with a -9.1 CPOE and an 17.9% bad-throw rate, so his floor is still there.

Some of the recent surge won't hold. A 10.3% TD rate over the last three games is a hot streak, not a new level, and his CPOE in that window (0.3) is barely above neutral, so the big numbers leaned on depth and red-zone finishes more than on pinpoint completion rates. Losing Jaylin Noel for the year also takes away his most efficient target per throw. The good news is that the Week 9 game, five touchdowns and 384 yards, came without him.

strengths.title: Vertical game is driving everything
strengths.body: His deep throws return 0.724 EPA per attempt with a +9.3 CPOE, and passes of 10-plus air yards account for most of his passing value. This is a deliberate shift: aggressiveness is up 6.3 points from 2025, and he's hitting those windows rather than forcing them. His rookie year showed the same downfield profile, so this looks like a return to his best version rather than a fluke.

strengths.title: Cleaner ball placement than ever
strengths.body: His bad-throw rate is 11.7%, ninth of 42, after three straight seasons ranking 46th or worse in that stat. Pairing that with a 2.3-point CPOE gain while throwing harder passes points to a genuine accuracy step. Of everything in his profile, this is the change most likely to stick.

strengths.title: Risk without the interceptions
strengths.body: Despite the aggressive approach, his interception rate is 0.7%, eighth in the league and 1.7 points under average. Only two turnover-worthy interceptions on the season backs that up. Some of it is luck, but he has been decisive on the deep shots rather than reckless.

concerns.title: Little help underneath or on the ground
concerns.body: Throws behind the line have cost 12.6 EPA, and the Houston run game ranks 25th in EPA, so drives stall when he isn't pushing the ball. Xavier Hutchinson has drawn the second-most targets at just 0.053 EPA each. Noel's season-ending toe surgery removes his most efficient target per throw, and that likely funnels more looks to lower-efficiency options. This is an offense-wide issue rather than a Stroud flaw, but it caps his floor.

concerns.title: Sacks when the play dies
concerns.body: His pressure-to-sack rate is 29.4%, 23rd of 42. That is his career norm (30.9% and 29.9% in his first two years), which makes 2025's 22.1% the outlier. Eight of his sacks came on third down, a big reason his conversion rate sits at 36.4% despite strong accuracy there. He holds the ball looking for the shot, and that is the price of the vertical approach.

concerns.title: Recent TD rate is running hot
concerns.body: Ten touchdowns on 97 attempts over the last three games is a 10.3% TD rate, against 5.7% for the season. His CPOE over that span was only 0.3, and his interception rate climbed to 2.1%. Expect the scoring to come back toward his season level even if the efficiency holds.

trend.note: After three poor opening weeks, he has posted strong EPA in four of his last five games, with only a dud against the Giants in between. The Week 9 game in Los Angeles was his best of the year.

nextGame.headline: Stingy Browns pass defense, low total, and a script that may favor running
nextGame.body:
Cleveland is the kind of defense that limits Stroud's profile. It ranks ninth in pass EPA allowed, fifth in sack rate and 12th against deep throws, and it allows just 14.1 PPR points a game to quarterbacks, eighth-fewest. The weakness is on the ground: 29th in rush EPA and dead last in explosive runs allowed. Offenses lean run against them (pass rate 1.7 points under norm, 26th), and the 39.5 total is among the lowest he has seen.

Availability tilts the script further. Deshaun Watson is out with a concussion, so Cleveland's offense (25th in EPA, worst in QB hits allowed) may struggle to force Houston to throw. That makes the Texans 4.5-point favorites. Defensive tackle Maliek Collins, a 62%-snap interior rusher, is also out, which softens the pressure Stroud hates. On Houston's side, David Montgomery's groin injury removes the lead back at the very moment the Browns invite a run plan, and Noel is gone for the year.

keyMatchups.title: Deep shots against a disciplined secondary
keyMatchups.body: His deep EPA of 0.724 is the engine of his season, and Cleveland allows 0.219 EPA on deep throws, 12th in the league. If the Browns keep the ball in front of them, he'll have to win underneath, where his offense has been weakest.

keyMatchups.title: Nico Collins vs. Cleveland's WR1 coverage
keyMatchups.body: Collins returns 0.666 EPA per target, the best of anyone with real volume. Cleveland holds lead receivers to 0.14 EPA per target, eighth-stingiest. Whoever wins this matchup decides whether Stroud's efficiency survives the tougher draw.

keyMatchups.title: Browns pass rush minus Collins
keyMatchups.body: Cleveland's sack rate ranks fifth, and Stroud's pressure-to-sack rate is 29.4%. Losing an interior starter helps, but drive-killing sacks remain the likeliest way this game goes sideways for him.

nextGame.watch: Whether Houston keeps attacking downfield on early downs once it has a lead, or leans on a depleted run game against Cleveland's soft run defense and caps Stroud's volume.

restOfSeason.body:
The accuracy gain and the willingness to push the ball look sustainable. Both mark a clear break from his 2024-25 profile, and they line up with his strong rookie season. Volume should stay healthy because Houston's defense gives up explosive passes at the league's worst rate, which keeps games open. Expect something like 245-290 passing yards a game. The touchdown rate should settle well below the recent run, around 1.6-2.3 a game, and the interception luck may give back a little.

The drag is the cast. Without Noel and with a weak run game, more of the burden lands on Collins, Boutte and Schultz, and on Stroud converting third-and-long, which hasn't been a strength. Efficiency of roughly 0.10-0.22 EPA per dropback is a reasonable band, below his last-five peak but above his season-long 2025 level. Rushing stays a non-factor.
swingFactors: How the target tree absorbs Noel's loss
Whether the run game can stabilize once Montgomery returns

confidence.note: An eight-game sample with a clear skill change, but Noel's loss reshapes his targets.
